statements.quote: The data that support the findings of this study are available from the corresponding author upon reasonable request. The data are not publicly available due to privacy or ethical restrictions.
statements.locator: PDF p. 23, DATA AVAILABILITY, complete paragraph (saved arXiv v3).

statements.quote: The study investigated how undetectable AI teammates with distinct personas shape learner agency and collaborative creative reasoning during a fast-paced story-generation activity (Appendix A).
statements.locator: PDF p. 7, Section 3.2, opening sentence; points to task materials in Appendix A, p. 28.

statements.quote: All tasks were administered via a custom-built online chat interface (Figure 1). Messages from both human and AI teammates were timestamped and logged, allowing fine-grained temporal, structural, and clustering analyses of collaborative discourse (Sections 3.6–3.8).
statements.locator: PDF p. 8, Section 3.2, final paragraph, first two sentences; interface and logged-data description, without a release link.

statements.quote: Both personas drew upon identical task knowledge, differing only in stance and communicative approach (Appendix B).
statements.locator: PDF p. 9, Section 3.3, second paragraph; points to persona prompts in Appendix B, pp. 28-30.

statements.quote: The creative-regulatory coding framework (Table 1) was adapted from established models of collaborative knowledge construction and creative reasoning.
statements.locator: PDF p. 9, Section 3.4, opening sentence; points to the coding framework in Table 1, p. 10.

statements.quote: Two independent raters were trained on the coding manual and jointly coded an initial 20% of the dataset (576 utterances) to establish a shared understanding of category boundaries.
statements.locator: PDF p. 9, Section 3.4, final paragraph; mentions a coding manual but gives no separate file or availability statement for it.

statements.quote: Specifically, we implemented SPM using the PrefixSpan algorithm (Han et al., 2001) through the official PrefixSpan Python API.
statements.locator: PDF p. 11, Section 3.7, first paragraph; software used, without study-code availability or a repository URL.

statements.quote: We estimated GMM solutions for k = 2 to k = 8 clusters using the Expectation-Maximization algorithm as implemented in scikit-learn.
statements.locator: PDF p. 12, Section 3.8, second paragraph; software used, without a study-code release.

statements.quote: All clustering procedures and subsequent statistical analyses were conducted in Python 3.12 using numpy, pandas, scikit-learn, and scikit-learn-extra.
statements.locator: PDF p. 13, Section 3.8, final sentence; software environment, without study-code availability.

notes: Checked on 2026-10-09. Read the complete 126015-character markdown conversion, including acknowledgments, references, and Appendices A-B. Verified the data-availability paragraph and relevant materials/software passages against text extracted from the saved 30-page PDF with PyMuPDF. Source is arXiv:2512.18239v3, 26 Jul 2026; the public arXiv landing page also lists v3 as the latest version. The paper explicitly says data are available from the corresponding author on reasonable request and are not public because of privacy or ethical restrictions. No data, code, preregistration, external repository, or separate supplementary-file URL is given; forms/c387.json data_and_code contains empty data_url and code_url strings. Appendix A (p. 28) supplies the task instructions; Appendix B (pp. 28-30) supplies both AI persona prompts. The coding framework appears in Table 1 (p. 10). Statements about the chat interface, coding manual, and analysis software identify methods/materials but do not offer their source code or a downloadable dataset. No relevant data/code repository was found, so deposits is empty; the manuscript, its embedded materials, unrelated search results, and blocked publisher page are not counted as data deposits. No participant data file was available to inspect, and no row counts, columns, arm assignments, outcome scores, text availability, file inventories, or data license could be confirmed for a deposit. Thus the missing total/per-arm creativity-analysis counts and exclusions, DSI change means/SDs/SEs, condition coefficients, and group-clustered robustness results in final.open_items cannot be computed from confirmed public data; participant-text diversity measures also cannot be computed. Whether a separate publisher supplement exists remains unresolved because Wiley returned HTTP 403 with a bot check. This limits confidence in the current-public-availability search despite the unambiguous on-request statement in the saved paper. All requests used urllib with User-Agent atlas-screening/0.1, without credentials, contact email, or requester identifiers. No account, access request, author contact, or bot-check bypass was attempted. No research data were saved to disk. Additional paper/search-result URL checks: https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.18239v3: HTTP 200; https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.18239: HTTP 200; http://dx.doi.org/10.1016/j.lcsi.2021.100539: HTTP 200, redirected to https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/S2210656121000507; http://dx.doi.org/10.3389/fpsyg.2017.01997: HTTP 200, redirected to https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/psychology/articles/10.3389/fpsyg.2017.01997/full; https://wileyonlinelibrary.com/journal/: HTTP 403, redirected to https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/. The two reference DOI links concern other studies, not c387 data; the malformed/wrapped cognitive-load DOI in the markdown was recovered from the PDF hyperlink. The generic Wiley footer also returned a bot check and was not pursued. The arXiv pages contain no author-supplied data-deposit link; generic sharing links are not evidence of deposited research data.
